learnings:
**Running notes (as of 2026-10-05, 40 closed picks, P&L -$116.58, win 45%)**

**State:** Exits are the strongest part (actual avg 0.94x vs hold-24h 0.24x vs hold-72h 0.075x). Do not touch stop/trail/no-move. Safety rules look protective overall (rejects: 75% rug, 5% doubled). **Weights:** momentum and holders were both set to 0.75 on 9-30 (by Ray). Only 14-17 picks since, net negative. Do not judge until about 20+ post-change picks. Holders component is inverted: high holders rug 90% vs 58% low (n=730). If still bad next week with more data, cut holders to 0.5.

**Scoring:** buckets not monotonic (70-79 best: rug 61%, median 0.11; 80+ rug 79%, median 0.04). Buyer_breadth maxed by 91% of coins, useless without a tighter threshold (owner). Safety rules look tight overall: 75% of rejects rugged and only 5% doubled. The problem is the **picks** that passed, with a 76% rug rate. That is no better than the rejects, so the current rules don't separate good from bad among survivors. I'm not proposing any loosening.

## 4. Scoring
- **Buckets are not monotonic.** 70–79 is best (rug 61%, median 0.11). 80+ is worse (rug 79%, median 0.04). Below 70 the buckets are also poor. Doubled rates are flat at 14–15% from 60 up, so score adds almost nothing.
- **Holders** is the only component with a strong split, and it is inverted. High holders: rug 90%, median 0.01. Low holders: rug 58%, median 0.14. It is full-marks for 41% of coins. The weight is already cut to 0.75, and 14 picks since the cut (9-30) are still net negative, so it's too early to judge.
- **Liquidity:** high scores beat low ones (rug 64% vs 86%). This is the one sensible component. 67% of coins get full marks.
- **Buyer_breadth:** 91% of coins get full marks, so it can't discriminate. That is a threshold problem. High vs low (73% vs 58% rug) is weak, and n=62 on the low side.
- **Momentum:** high is slightly worse (rug 78% vs 68%), no real separation on doubling.
- **Social:** high is worse on doubling (4% vs 14%, n=51). Small n.
- **Survival:** high is slightly better (rug 60% vs 73%, n=89). Weak.
- **Claude PICK vs PASS:** pick median 24h is 0.04 and pass is 0.08. Pick rug rate is 76% vs 65% for pass, and picks doubled less (6% vs 15%, n=33 vs 301). Stage 3 is **not adding value**, and may be subtracting it.
- **Entry signal, 5-min spike over 20%:** yes (n=79) vs no (n=540). Down 40% at 1h is 53% vs 48%, up 50% at 1h is 11% vs 12%, median 24h is 0.09 vs 0.06. There is no meaningful separation, so I'm not recommending it.

## 5. Exits
Actual exits average **0.942×**. Holding 24h averages 0.242× and holding 72h averages 0.075×. The exit stack is the strongest part of the system: it turns a market where most coins go to zero into a roughly break-even outcome. Stops often fill near 0.57×, close to the −40% line. The remaining losses come from coins that dump immediately after entry. I'm not changing exit parameters.

## 6. Go-live checklist
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| ≥ 30 closed picks | **Pass** (40) |
| Total P&L positive | **Fail** (−$116.59) |
| Win rate ≥ 35% | **Pass** (45%) |
| Profitable in 2 of last 3 weeks | **Fail** (−32 / −34 / −50) |
| Claude picks beat passes | **Fail** (0.04 vs 0.08) |

## 7. Changes this week
**No changes.** The last weight edits (9-30, by Ray) are only 5 days old, and I need to see their effect on at least 20 new picks. The signals that look actionable, a lower holders weight and a higher min_score, don't have clean evidence. The score ordering isn't monotonic, so raising min_score would not help. Exits are working, and safety rules are protective. Next week's check is whether 80+ buckets and the holders-weighted picks improve.
